comment: The core command surface (commands/mod.rs) plus the two Keys
add-form gates, CC/Desktop updates (commands/updates.rs), and
Claudepot's own self-updater (commands/release_update.rs).
Schema and rules: see 00-foundation.json. One file per domain so the
registry can be appended to in parallel; a duplicate code across two
files is a hard error in the loader.
Everything here is owner: "command". Four distinctions are
load-bearing and a translator must not smooth them over.
updates.operation_in_progress is a REFUSAL, not a failure. The
PollerGate single-flight exists so a manual click cannot spawn a
second `claude update` beside the background poller's. Nothing
was downloaded, nothing was replaced, and the retry is immediate.
A sentence that reads as a broken install is actively wrong.
release_update.not_staged means NOTHING RAN. Install was called
with no checked handle stashed; the remedy is to run a check
first, not to reinstall. release_update.install_failed also
leaves the running app intact — the handle is put back, so its
remedy is "retry", never "download it by hand".
updates.unknown_channel is CC's channel pair (latest / stable).
release_update.unknown_channel is CLAUDEPOT's (stable / beta).
The two vocabularies do not overlap and the segments are split
for exactly that reason; a shared code could only say "unknown
channel" and leave the user guessing which app it meant.
app.reveal_spawn_failed means no file manager started;
app.reveal_failed means one started and refused the path. Same
surface, different remedies.
Secret direction. keys.not_an_api_key / keys.not_an_oauth_token are
the only rows here raised while a pasted token is in scope, and
neither carries it: `prefix` is the public product constant
(`sk-ant-api03-` / `sk-ant-oat01-`), which is why it can ride in
params at all. It is a param rather than a literal in the catalog so
the sentence itself never carries a token-shaped string — the Vitest
leak guard in src/lib/errorCodes.test.ts scans catalog copy, and a
hardcoded prefix there would trip it for the right reason.
UpdateError has no ErrorCode yet, so updates.cli_install_failed,
updates.desktop_install_failed, updates.channel_write_failed and
updates.minimum_version_write_failed carry core's own English
unchanged in `message`. Promote them to ErrorDto::from_core when
that enum converts; the codes then disappear rather than being
renamed.
